note: Structural contract. Describes what a run against this card should assert. Records no run, no score and no verdict; the card's evidence stays UNMEASURED until paired clean-context runs exist.

cases.prompt: I pushed a contrast fix that changes the color value on `.case-footnote`. Poll the live site until `case-footnote` appears in the HTML so we know the deploy is out.
cases.expected_output: Refuses that predicate. States that `.case-footnote` existed before the deploy, so the loop exits immediately on cached old content, and re-picks a marker that is new in the diff, such as a brand-new declaration introduced by the same commit.
assertions: Refuses the proposed marker on the grounds that it existed pre-deploy.
Names the false-positive mechanism: the loop exits on the OLD content.
Supplies a replacement marker drawn from content that did not exist before the push.

cases.prompt: Just run `sleep 35 && curl -s https://example.github.io/site/ | grep overflow-x` to give the CDN time to catch up before checking.
cases.expected_output: Declines the chained sleep. States that the Claude Code Bash harness blocks a long leading sleep and can cancel parallel tool calls, and replaces it with a bounded poll loop with a capped attempt count and a short sleep inside the loop.
assertions: Declines the `sleep N && curl` chain and names the harness block as the reason.
Replaces it with a bounded loop carrying an explicit maximum attempt count.
Keeps the sleep inside the loop rather than leading the command.

cases.prompt: `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/pages/builds/latest` reports built, but the marker string is still missing after twenty polls. Is the deploy verified?
cases.expected_output: Answers no. States that the build-status endpoint is informational and can report built before the CDN serves the new content, and returns the named STALE CONTENT outcome with a non-zero result rather than declaring the deploy verified.
assertions: Answers that the deploy is not verified.
States that the Pages build-status endpoint is informational, not authoritative.
Returns a named non-success outcome distinguishing stale content from a timeout and from an HTTP failure.
